native_retrieval.title: Aam Aadmi Party (AAP) | Formation, Ideology, Elections, & Facts | Britannica
native_retrieval.snippet: The Aam Aadmi Party (AAP) is a political party in India founded in November 2012 by Arvind Kejriwal following an anti-corruption movement in India in 2011. The AAP has served as the ruling party in Delhi and Punjab. It has also won seats in the legislative assemblies in Gujarat, Jammu and Kashmir, and Goa. In 2015, the AAP won the Delhi Legislative Assembly elections with a landslide victory, securing 67 out of 70 seats. The Aam Aadmi Party (AAP), or "Common Man's Party," was formed by Arvind Kejriwal in November 2012. The AAP has served as the ruling party in Delhi and Punjab, and has won seats in the legislative assemblies in Gujarat, Jammu and Kashmir, and Goa. In 2013, the AAP entered the political arena for the first time in the Delhi Legislative Assembly elections, emerging as the second-largest party. The Aam Aadmi Party (AAP), or Common Man’s Party, was formed in 2012 by Arvind Kejriwal in response to the 2011 anti-corruption movement in India.
